prompt: An evening theater box office, painted in opaque gouache. On the counter a small tangerine-orange paper admission ticket rests on a white cotton glove under indigo-violet light. The first thing one notices is the ticket: a compact, saturated shape with a crisp perforated paper edge against a relatively quiet violet-gray fold. A muted pearl-white lit patch, soft woven grain and dull tinted folds let the glove read as white cotton. Keep the evening ticket window recognizable in understated, low-contrast brush shapes. Matte overlapping gouache strokes on paper.

A transparent watercolor of a teahouse windowsill at sunset. One small red raspberry rests on a pale celadon glazed plate catching amber window light. Let the berry catch the eye immediately: a concentrated spot of red with a few small defined drupelets on a softly washed pale turquoise plane. Leave the plate's own light blue-green body color visible beside a gentle amber reflection and a delicate shaded glaze. Use luminous transparent washes, gentle blooms and paper showing through. Understate the window and its sunset glow.

A colored-pencil drawing of a carpenter's bench under a blue work light. A small yellow carpenter's pencil is tucked into the pocket of a black leather tool pouch; its flat yellow shaft and sharpened end emerge above the pocket opening. Let this small, clear yellow shape on charcoal leather be the first read. Restrained blue reflections across softly burnished black leather, an understated seam and dark leather grain show the pouch material. Layered colored pencil hatching on toothed paper, quieter marks over the worn workbench.

An intimate natural still-life photograph in a kitchen at blue dawn. A single small green olive rests on a shallow copper tray. The olive is the first object to catch the eye, a clearly focused, softly glistening green form and its small contact shadow against a quiet brushed copper plane. Soft blue light comes from the kitchen window, with enough muted copper-orange body reflection in the tray to identify the metal. Subdue the brightest metal reflections and background detail. A close, slightly elevated three-quarter view, natural optical falloff.

A soft pastel drawing of a dressing room in the pink light before a performance. One small silver dragonfly brooch is pinned to the side of a navy felt hat. Give the four delicate wings and slim dragonfly body the clearest marks, with a restrained silvery glint against a patch of deep navy so the brooch attracts the eye first. The hat keeps its own navy blue under muted pink reflected light; soft dry pastel scumbling and broken short marks suggest its fuzzy felt surface. A quiet blurred impression of the dressing room behind it.
